body:
Large AI matches repeatedly scan mostly empty building arrays and serialize Maxima's large continuation state through individual virtual writes. This reuses Cortex's placement snapshot for the remaining building-distance checks, rejects undiscovered candidates before footprint checks, and buffers Maxima's existing binary field encoding in 16 KiB chunks. Candidate order, field encoding, saved caches and version gates are unchanged.

Automated/headless and scripted test runs now default autosaving off without changing persisted preferences. Explicit initial/checkpoint/final saves remain available; harnesses can opt in after loading. Interactive autosaves move from roughly 10 seconds to 60 seconds at normal speed, with the first-save phase unchanged. This reduces interruptions but increases the play between recovery snapshots.

### Measured combined effect

8,192 ticks on the same 256×256 eight-team map; game seed 41, map seed 20260914, symmetric-arena generator 15. Explicit final save included; telemetry disabled. CPU time is user + system.

| Match | Baseline CPU seconds | Changed CPU seconds | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mixed eight AIs | 23.01 | 12.15 | 47% |
| Eight Cortex AIs | 51.88 | 22.55 | 57% |

Single runs on a shared macOS ARM64 host with concurrent build activity: workload-specific results, not universal speedups. These measure the combined batch, including skipped autosaves; serializer gains and save-skipping gains must not be added independently.

### Verification and limits

- macOS and Linux ARM64 release builds pass. Full per-tick records match baseline for 4,096-tick mixed-eight-AI and four-Maxima games; changed Linux/macOS traces and final saves match exactly.
- 86,400 exhaustive Cortex geometry comparisons pass, including wrapped footprints, live/dead/null-type buildings and swarm/inn filters.
- Binary bytes and SHA1 match the scalar serializer across nested containers, signed limits, 64-bit ordering, strings, buffer boundaries and interleaved direct writes. Text fallback matches. This regression also runs in Linux and Windows CI.
- Autosave regression passes on macOS/Linux: default off, explicit opt-in, configured cadence, atomic failure preservation, reload and unchanged preference files.
- The longer timing runs have matching final save contents except the existing header SHA1 affected by save history. No format/version changes.
- Baseline and changed checkpoint-resumed Maxima runs match for 2,048 ticks. Both retain a pre-existing discrepancy against uninterrupted execution beginning at tick 2048; this PR does not fix that issue.
- Windows/x86 per-tick execution comparison was not performed; CI serialization tests are narrower coverage.

[Validation archive](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/275256f62/test/fixtures/ai-save-performance/validation-20260914.tar.gz) (7.8 MiB) and [SHA256 index](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/275256f62/test/fixtures/ai-save-performance/validation-20260914.index.json) contain exact commands, input maps/saves, representative output saves, full per-tick record summaries, timings and test logs. Temporary profiling and feasibility documents are excluded.
title: Reduce AI placement and save overhead in large matches
